title: Normality from geometric conjugations in a smooth ambient group
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups below are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$; subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $J$ be smooth, let $N\subseteq J$ be a closed subgroup, and let $\bar k$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of $k$. If every $g\in J(\bar k)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Int}(g)(N_{\bar k})=N_{\bar k}$ as closed subgroup schemes of $J_{\bar k}$, then $N$ is normal in $J$. Here $\operatorname{Int}(g)$ is the group-scheme automorphism $x\mapsto gxg^{-1}$, and normality means $jN(A)j^{-1}=N(A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $j\in J(A)$. Neither $N$ nor $J$ is required to be connected; no smoothness of $N$ is required. The hypothesis concerns equality of subgroup schemes, rather than just equality of their sets of geometric points.

source.place: Corollary 1.85 and its normalizer proof, printed p.32, applied over an algebraic closure; Proposition 1.90, printed p.33, applies it to weakly characteristic subgroups. Smoothness of the ambient group is essential in the normalizer proof.

proof.text: Write $J=\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion], $N=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ for an ideal $I$. Both are separated over $k$: for any affine $\operatorname{Spec}B$, its relative diagonal corresponds to the surjection $B\otimes_kB\to B$, $b\otimes c\mapsto bc$, hence is closed by the same criterion and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. They are finite type by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $R$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Thus all the separatedness and finite-type hypotheses needed for the factorization-locus theorem hold.

source.place: Corollary 1.85, printed p.32; Proposition 1.83 and its transporter construction, pp.30–32. The closed one-sided transporter is supplied by the existing constant-source factorization-locus theorem (Theorem 1.105, pp.37–38).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-constant-source-closed-factorization-locus] with $Y=N$, $X=S=J$, $W=N$, and $f:N\times_kJ\to J$ given by $(n,j)\mapsto jnj^{-1}$. This is a morphism by the group-scheme operations [def-sc-group-scheme]. Obtain a closed subscheme $L\hookrightarrow J$ such that, for every $k$-scheme $T$, a map $j:T\to J$ factors through $L$ exactly when the whole morphism $N\times_kT\to J$ given by conjugation by $j$ factors through $N$. This tests subgroup schemes, including their nilpotents. The theorem also identifies the locus after scalar extension with $L_{\bar k}$. We need only this one-sided transporter; equality will follow by applying it to inverses.

source.place: Corollary 1.85, printed p.32; Proposition 1.83 and its transporter construction, pp.30–32. The closed one-sided transporter is supplied by the existing constant-source factorization-locus theorem (Theorem 1.105, pp.37–38).

proof.text: For every $g\in J(\bar k)$, the assumed equality $\operatorname{Int}(g)(N_{\bar k})=N_{\bar k}$ implies the factorization tested in step 2. Therefore $L_{\bar k}(\bar k)=J_{\bar k}(\bar k)$. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], smoothness of $J/k$ makes $J_{\bar k}$ reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] it has coordinate algebra $R\otimes_k\bar k$, generated over $\bar k$ by the images of the finite set of generators of $R$. The immersion $L_{\bar k}\hookrightarrow J_{\bar k}$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] it is cut out by an ideal $K$ of $R\otimes_k\bar k$. Each $a\in K$ evaluates to zero at every $\bar k$-point, so clause 2 of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] gives $a=0$. Hence $K=0$ and $L_{\bar k}=J_{\bar k}$ as schemes. Reducedness is used only for the ambient group.

source.place: Corollary 1.85, printed p.32; Proposition 1.83 and its transporter construction, pp.30–32. The closed one-sided transporter is supplied by the existing constant-source factorization-locus theorem (Theorem 1.105, pp.37–38).

proof.text: Again by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion], write $L=\operatorname{Spec}(R/H)$ over $J$. Its quotient map kills every $h\in H$. After tensoring with $\bar k$ the map is an isomorphism by step 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], so $h\otimes1=0$ in $R\otimes_k\bar k$. To see this forces $h=0$, take a $k$-basis of $\bar k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free]. The finite expansion of $1$ in this basis has a nonzero coefficient $c$; the associated coordinate functional divided by $c$ is a $k$-linear map $\lambda:\bar k\to k$ with $\lambda(1)=1$. The map $r\otimes a\mapsto r\lambda(a)$ is well-defined by bilinearity and sends $h\otimes1$ to $h$. Thus $H=0$ and $L=J$. This is the explicit linear-algebra descent, requiring no perfection assumption on $k$.

source.place: Corollary 1.85, printed p.32; Proposition 1.83 and its transporter construction, pp.30–32. The closed one-sided transporter is supplied by the existing constant-source factorization-locus theorem (Theorem 1.105, pp.37–38).

proof.text: Let $A$ be any commutative $k$-algebra and $j\in J(A)$. Since $L=J$, the criterion of step 2 applied to $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ shows that conjugation by $j$ carries $N_A$ into itself. Evaluating on $A$-points gives $jN(A)j^{-1}\subseteq N(A)$. Apply the same criterion to $j^{-1}$ to obtain $j^{-1}N(A)j\subseteq N(A)$, and conjugate this inclusion by $j$ to get the reverse inclusion $N(A)\subseteq jN(A)j^{-1}$. Equality holds for every $A,j$, which is normality by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Arbitrary $A$, including nonreduced algebras, was allowed by the cited locus criterion; neither connectedness nor smoothness of $N$ entered.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q81-1446788c4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all five steps and every cited statement in full and found no faults, so I made no changes. Source: Milne iAG2017 Cor 1.85 (p.32, with Prop 1.83/1.84). The item is the case k' = k̄ and matches it hypothesis by hypothesis: J smooth, N closed with no smoothness assumed, stability as schemes, normality on all A-points. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, there are no new nodes, and no re-split note exists for this item. Step 1: the 01QO criterion and fibre-product-affine-spectra give N = Spec(R/I) and separatedness through the surjective diagonal; lft-affine-pairs gives R finitely generated, so the locus theorem's hypotheses hold. Step 2: the statement of lem-sfb-constant-source-closed-factorization-locus with Y=W=N, X=S=J and f=(n,j)↦jnj⁻¹ gives the closed one-sided transporter L (Milne's T_G(H,H)). Step 3: T = Spec k̄ shows every k̄-point lies in L. J_k̄ is reduced by sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced, the defining ideal K comes from closed-immersion base change, and clause 2 of the Nullstellensatz node (not clause 3) gives K = 0. Step 4: an explicit k-linear retraction λ with λ(1)=1 from a basis of k̄ gives H = 0 with no perfectness needed; elementary is justified. Step 5: L = J at T = Spec A gives jN(A)j⁻¹ ⊆ N(A), and applying it to j⁻¹ gives equality, which is normality as in def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup. Route: the two nodes from other units (smooth geometric reducedness, Nullstellensatz) are both Lean-closed in slopmaster2, so they count as tools and no tool_uses entry is needed; there is no cycle. Duplicates: lem-sfb-galois-descent-affine-subgroups needs a Galois extension, and no node states Milne 1.85. Edge cases: N=J, N=e, disconnected finite J, α_p⊂G_a, and the non-smooth α_p⋊G_m counterexample showing smoothness is needed. Minor: the report mentions a citations.json the commit does not contain; no rule requires it.
